cells.title: Let git fetch, a push of main, and config.json staging through the guards
cells.action: GitHub issues #131 and #135 (read them with `gh issue view 131` and `gh issue view 135`). Red first; name EVERY new test with `issue_131` or `issue_135`. #131: with phase idle in the main checkout, the intake gate (logic in hooks/write_guard/checks.rs evaluate_git_invocation ~793-934: READONLY ~860, idle_gate_safe_form ~1263, push deny ~873-880; the message only at paths.rs:592) refuses `git fetch` and `git push origin main`. Make `git fetch` (any remote, any flags) read-only-eligible, and make `git push <remote> main` (and `HEAD:main`) bookkeeping-eligible on main. Keep refused and pin with tests: `git push origin main:other`, `git push origin HEAD~1:main`, `git push origin +main`, `--force`/`-f`/`--force-with-lease`/`--mirror`/`--delete`, `git push origin :main`, `git push -o ...`, `git -c x=y push ...`, `git pull`, every other unmodelled git subcommand, and the outward arm that refuses push from a linked worktree (checks.rs ~1033). The existing assertions at write_guard/tests.rs ~1825-1827 and ~2859-2861 pin the old refusal of `git push origin main` on idle main; D1 reverses exactly that, so update those two and only those two. #135: in a granted feature worktree, `git add .bee/config.json` becomes a shell target (guards.rs ~841-868; config.json is not a CLI-store exemption, guards.rs ~66-88) and main.rs ~633-650 denies it (`cannot be modified via the shell`). Reproduce first: `git commit` may add no targets and already pass. Staging and committing are not content writes: let `git add`/`git commit` naming .bee/config.json through, while anything that changes the file's bytes stays refused and is pinned: redirect, sed -i, tee, cp, mv over it, `git checkout -- .bee/config.json`, `git restore`, `git rm`, `git mv`, and a compound `git add .bee/config.json && echo x > .bee/config.json`. Tests must pin both the newly allowed shapes and the still-refused neighbours. Do not change any other guard. No code comments.

git push origin main on an idle main checkout is not refused; a force push or a push of another ref still is
git add .bee/config.json in a granted worktree is not refused; a shell redirect into .bee/config.json still is

cells.title: Accept cells cap --report-file in the CLI-shape guard
cells.action: GitHub issue #130 (`gh issue view 130`). cells.title: Dispatch escalated cells under v2 plans and let escalate --off clear
cells.action: GitHub issue #134 (`gh issue view 134`). Red first; name EVERY new test with `escalate_v2`, and put them inline in the files this cell owns (not verbs/cells/tests.rs or verbs/drivers/tests.rs, which other work may touch). Two defects: (1) under an approved bee-plan/v2 role plan, an escalated cell gets a `[bee-tier: ceiling]` payload from dispatch prepare, and the model guard refuses it with planned_role_mismatch (model_guard.rs ~811) because only the planned role is accepted. An escalated cell must dispatch: either the guard accepts the escalation marker for a cell whose record says escalated, or prepare emits a payload the guard accepts — pick the one that keeps the planned-role check strict: model_guard.rs ~901-909 compares declared to effective_role, prepare.rs ~2223-2225 emits ceiling from cell_is_escalated (validate.rs:108); accept ceiling ONLY when cell_is_escalated(cell) is true. Pin refused: a non-escalated cell declaring ceiling; a cell with role ceiling but no escalate flag (the self-escalation hole prepare.rs ~2226-2250 names); an escalated cell declaring a third role. (2) `bee cells escalate --id X --off` is refused as unsupported argument shape, and `--off true` leaves escalate true and re-runs the budget check. Reproduce first, then fix both so `--off`, `--off true` and `--off=true` clear the escalation without the budget check; update the PINNED_FLAG_COUNT pin in catalog.rs only if the distinct flag-name set changes. No code comments.

a non-escalated cell declaring a role other than its planned role is still refused
bee cells escalate --id X --off clears the escalation without a budget check

prohibitions: No weakening of the planned-role check for non-escalated cells

cells.title: Report a paseo spawn timeout with a live agent as running
cells.action: GitHub issue #129 (`gh issue view 129`). Red first; name EVERY new test with `spawn_timeout`. On the paseo transport, `bee herding run` returns outcome spawn_failed, retryable true, remedy unclaim, when the paseo CLI times out after 15s, while the agent was in fact created and keeps running unsupervised; the retry remedy then invites a second agent on the same cell. Reproduce with the existing fake transport seam (see the test that returns `Err("paseo timed out after 15s")`, run.rs ~14369). Fix: on a spawn timeout, look the agent up by the name the run gave it (the transport's list/lookup); if found, continue supervising it as a normal running agent; if not found, keep spawn_failed. A spawn_failed outcome must never be retryable while an agent with that name exists. No code comments.

truths: a spawn timeout whose agent exists is supervised, not reported spawn_failed
a spawn timeout with no agent is still spawn_failed
spawn_failed is not retryable while an agent with that name exists
key_links: the lookup uses the same name the spawn used
prohibitions: No edit to any existing assertion

cells.action: GitHub issue #128 (`gh issue view 128`). Red first; name EVERY new test with `worktree_state_record` and put them inline in the files this cell owns. cells.action: GitHub issue #136 (`gh issue view 136`). Red first; name EVERY new test with `doctor_design_skill` and put them inline in doctor.rs.
